Layers 1 to 5, in order

The decision sheet

Twenty-five things to confirm and fifteen things that end the purchase, arranged so that failure stays cheap.

This is the framework as a working document. Answer layer 1 before doing anything else: if a stop condition there is true, none of the rest of this page applies to you. Each layer is meant to be settled before you spend money on the next one.

Your ticks are stored in this browser and nowhere else. There is no account, no form and no submission — if you want a record, print the page and keep it with your notes.

Work this layer out first: How to verify in person · Read the due-diligence checklist · Add up what closing costs

Print this page and take it to your lawyer. A ticked box is your own answer, not evidence — the sheet exists to show you which answers you have not actually checked.

What this sheet is not. It is not a legal opinion, a valuation, or a prediction. It does not tell you whether prices will rise. It is a way of finding out, in ten minutes and for nothing, whether a purchase you are considering fails on the first two layers — which is where most purchases by foreign buyers actually fail.

If you want the reasoning behind any line, follow it back to the framework. If you want the vocabulary you will hear at the counter, the glossary has the twenty-four terms that come up most often, with the characters you will see on paper.
